native.answer: The sensation of pain from a burn is carried by nerve fibers. These fibers also respond to temperature. Touching a room temperature (or even cool) object can temporarily “override” the pain signals traveling to the brain. Essentially, the cool sensation competes with and reduces the perception of the burn pain. It doesn’t *stop* the burn damage, just masks the feeling of pain for a short time. It's a temporary effect because the burn continues to injure the tissue, and the pain will return.
